conf.description: Palo Alto NGFW Config log (syslog-leef, PAN-OS 10.2/11.1), direct route: cribl-pack mechanism implemented natively (no Packs installed) as far as the map's own documented gap allows - splits the generic LEEF:Version|Vendor|Product|Version|EventID| header and key=value-parses the attribute body into whatever field names the device actually emits, but does NOT rename to ECS/custom because the work order itself could not render the exact LEEF attribute spellings for this log from the vendor schema reference.

conf.comment: paloalto-ngfw / config / syslog-leef. GAP, stated by the work order itself: 'the exact LEEF key spellings for the config log were not renderable from the vendor schema reference... validate the key names against a live device or the QRadar LEEF guide before pinning the pipeline.' This pipeline therefore does the structurally-generic half only - split the LEEF header, key=value-parse the attribute body (whatever keys are actually present) - and stops there rather than guessing vendor key names for admin/cmd/result/path/before-after-change-detail. It assumes the default LEEF whitespace/tab attribute delimiter since the optional 6th header field naming a custom delimiter, if present, is not distinguished from LEEF 1.0's 5-field form here. No secret-node redaction is applied because the before/after-change-detail key names (and therefore which fields to redact) are unknown; this is a real, documented residual risk, not an oversight, until the keys are confirmed against a live device.

functions.description: why ECS rename and XML redaction are NOT implemented here, per the work order's own stated gap

split the generic LEEF:Version|Vendor|Product|Version|EventID| header from the attribute body; does not attempt to distinguish an optional LEEF 2.0 custom-delimiter 6th field from the LEEF 1.0 5-field form, since the vendor's actual template choice is unconfirmed
generic key=value parse of the attribute body into whatever field names the device actually emits - the map does not document these spellings, so no rename to ECS/custom follows
tag the dataset; this is the only field this pipeline can populate with confidence given the unresolved key-name gap
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
